facts.statement: Stratesaurus is an extinct genus of small basal plesiosaurs found in the Early Jurassic of the United Kingdom.
facts.quote: Stratesaurus is an extinct genus of small-bodied basal plesiosaur known from the Early Jurassic period (most likely earliest Hettangian stage) of the United Kingdom.

facts.statement: The genus Stratesaurus contains only one known species, Stratesaurus taylori.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, S. taylori.

facts.statement: Stratesaurus had a skull length of 18 cm and a total body length of 2 meters.
facts.quote: It was a small plesiosaur, with a skull length of 18 cm and a body length of 2 m.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen OUMNH J.10337 consists of a nearly complete crushed skull and a partial postcranial skeleton with vertebrae, a hindlimb, and an ilium.
facts.quote: Stratesaurus is known from the holotype specimen OUMNH J.10337, a dorsoventrally crushed but nearly complete skull, and three-dimensionally preserved partial postcranial skeleton including anterior cervical and pectoral vertebrae, a partial hindlimb and ilium.

facts.statement: All known specimens of Stratesaurus were collected at Street, Somerset, from the Pre-Planorbis beds of the Blue Lias Formation.
facts.quote: All specimens were collected at Street, of Somerset, from the Pre-Planorbis beds of the Blue Lias Formation of the Lower Lias Group.

facts.statement: Stratesaurus lived approximately 199.6 to 198 million years ago during the earliest Hettangian stage, shortly after the Triassic-Jurassic boundary.
facts.quote: Thus, they probably fall within the earliest Hettangian P. tilmanni Chronozone, which is about 199.6-198 million years old, immediately following the Triassic–Jurassic Boundary.

facts.statement: Stratesaurus is considered one of the oldest known plesiosaurs because fossils found at its discovery site represent the earliest known occurrence of the group.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurs fossils which were discovered at Street represent the earliest known occurrence of the Plesiosauria. Hence, Stratesaurus is one of the oldest plesiosaurs to date.

facts.statement: Stratesaurus had an unconstricted snout with five tooth sockets in the premaxilla and sixteen in the maxilla.
facts.quote: Its snout is not constricted, and it has five of tooth sockets in its premaxilla and sixteen in the maxilla.

facts.statement: A unique feature of Stratesaurus is the strongly developed backwards-pointing projections on the prezygapophyses in the front part of the neck.
facts.quote: In the front part of the neck, there are strongly developed backwards-pointing projections on the prezygapophyses, an autapomorphy (unique derived feature) of the genus.

facts.statement: Stratesaurus is distinguished by the unusually short lengths of the vertebral bodies in the shoulder region.
facts.quote: Also autapomorphic are the short lengths of the centra (vertebral bodies) in the shoulder region.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Stratesaurus as the most basal member of the Rhomaleosauridae family.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis performed by Benson et al. (2012) found it to be the basalmost rhomaleosaurid.

facts.statement: Stratesaurus was first described and named by Benson, Evans, and Druckenmiller in 2012.
facts.quote: Stratesaurus was first described and named by Roger B. J. Benson, Mark Evans and Patrick S. Druckenmiller in 2012 and the type species is Stratesaurus taylori.

facts.statement: The genus name Stratesaurus combines "Strate", the historical name for Street from the Domesday Book, and the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from "Strate", the name for Street as it recorded in the Domesday Book and from Greek sauros, meaning "lizard".

facts.statement: The species name taylori honors paleontologist Michael A. Taylor for his work preparing the holotype specimen.
facts.quote: The specific name honors the paleontologist Michael A. Taylor, who performed acid preparation of the holotype.

facts.statement: Stratesaurus is classified within the order Plesiosauria, suborder Pliosauroidea, and family Rhomaleosauridae.
facts.quote: ordo: Plesiosauria subordo: Pliosauroidea familia: Rhomaleosauridae

facts.statement: The fossil record for Stratesaurus spans from 201.4 to 199.5 million years ago during the Hettangian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Hettangian (201.4 to 199.5 million years ago)
